title: Actual completion unit on a strict K-flat quotient cone
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $W$ under consideration assume $\ell$ invertible on $W$, use its small pro-etale site in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $W$ be such a scheme, let $N\in D(\widehat R_W)$, and let $q:Q\to N$ be any flat-term K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W} B_{W,n}$, $r_n(z)=z\otimes1$ and $\tau_n=1\otimes(B_{W,n+1}\to B_{W,n})$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the strict quotient-semilinear system category on the ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], let $TQ=(Q_n,\tau_n)$, and let $D=U_W(TQ)$ be its restriction to strict towers of $\widehat R_W$-modules. Write $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, $\mathcal L_W=R\lim U_W$, for the canonical simultaneous derived reduction/limit adjunction, with actual unit $u_N$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For a strict tower complex $Z$ put $H(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Z)[-1]$, $s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1})$, with coordinates and differential
$$H(Z)^i=(\prod_n Z_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod_n Z_n^i),\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da).$$
Use the normalized Roos identification $\rho_D:H(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WN$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

The strict augmentation $v_Q:Q\to H(D)$, $v_Q(z)=(0,(r_nz)_n)$, is a chain map and satisfies
$$u_N=\rho_D[v_Q][q]^{-1}.$$
This equality is of entire derived morphisms, with zero shifted-product coordinate. More precisely, for any K-injective resolutions with injective terms $a:TQ\to I$ on the ringed sequence site and $j:U_WI\to J$ on its constant-ring tower site [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], the composite
$$Q\longrightarrow\lim U_WI\xrightarrow{\lim j}\lim J,\qquad z\longmapsto(a_nr_nz)_n\longmapsto(j_na_nr_nz)_n$$
represents the actual unit after $[q]^{-1}$. The first arrow is the ordinary-adjunction transpose of $a$ for $T\dashv\lim U_W$, and the second is the normalized right-derived composition comparison for restriction of rings followed by sequence projection. Under the canonical inclusion $\lim J\to H(J)$ with zero shifted coordinate, this composite equals $H(jU_W(a))v_Q$. The unit formula is independent of all these resolutions and natural for morphisms of $N$ in the derived category. No completeness or boundedness assumption on $N$ is made.

proof.text: Take compatible S, coherence, M and D from the canonical-model construction lemma. The theorem below only combines these data; no representative or resolution is chosen in this step.

The termwise adjunction transpose of a is the unit followed by ordinaryLimit(a); naturality of M.limitComparison gives transpose(a)=augmentation followed by lim(tower(a)). Taking degree p and using limitComparison_projection and unit_tensor gives the stated local-section formula.

The cone augmentation is augmentation followed by roosι. The formula roosι_χ and biproduct/product extensionality give the zero shifted coordinate. Naturality of roosι twice gives the strict chain identity for every a and j.

Apply D.hom_normalization to the identity of quotient(Q). Its transpose is the ordinary unit. Substitute D.systemUnit_composition and D.roos_normalization, and cancel the invertible reductionComparison on Q. This gives the whole unit formula on Q. Naturality of the actual adjunction unit transports it through every representative isomorphism q.

For K-injective J, limitUnit_normalization makes D.limitUnit(J) invertible; roos_normalization then makes Q(roosι J) invertible. Define eCone by this map. Define eI from M.limitComparison inverse and D.systemUnit, and eJ from D.limitUnit(J) followed by the inverses of Q(j) and the exact-restriction comparison. Naturality of D.limitUnit and systemUnit_composition give Q(lim j)eJ=eI. Both eI and eJ are invertible, so lim j is a quasi-isomorphism.

Naturality of D.roos, its inclusion normalization, and naturality of exact-restriction localization yield the displayed completionComparison resolution equality. Localize the strict chain identity, cancel eCone and both resolution/left-comparison isomorphisms, and substitute the unit formula already proved. This gives the full two-resolution formula for arbitrary a,j,q. Finally use the naturality equation of S.adjunction.unit for every derived morphism.

proof_origin.place: Original steps 1--4 are isolated as the canonical-model construction. The Lean proof establishes all remaining whole-unit, chain-cone, two-resolution and naturality assertions by adjunction normalization, naturality and cancellation, preserving the unit route.

tool_uses.why: Exact products of arbitrary pro-etale module sheaves supply the hypothesis of the strict Roos comparison; this is a generic site tool, not a replacement of trace transport.
The generic exact-product tower comparison identifies the explicit cone and its zero-coordinate augmentation with total derived inverse limit.
Unbounded resolutions on small ringed sites supply the two simultaneous injective models.
Generic ringed sequence adjunction supplies the flat representative and the actual ordinary-transpose normalization.
Generic resolving-class adjunction tool identifies the transpose of the resolved identity with the actual derived unit.
Generic composition theorem supplies the normalized map lim(j) without assuming restriction preserves K-injectives.
Generic sequence projection comparison identifies the transported derived adjunction with reduction/limit.
Existing simultaneous derived coefficient adjunction identifies the named functors and supplies naturality of their unit.

Step 2: ordinary transpose formulas and the transition identity checked. Step 3: the sequence-projection fraction extension plus the resolving normalization give unit=[b][q]^{-1}, with no K-injectivity preservation needed. Step 4: the composition theorem gives that lim j represents kappa. Step 5: dv_Q=(0,gamma dz) and H(f)v_Q=iota_J b' recomputed. Step 6: Roos normalization rho_D=[iota_J]^{-1}[H(f)] and cancellation by an isomorphism. Step 7: naturality.
